text:
Alex M.: Quick UX question — on the latest console mock the chart legend stretches too far on narrow panels when there are 8+ series. Feels noisy and pushes the plot area down.
Priya S.: Yeah I noticed that too on small team dashboards. Options: wrap to multiple rows, collapse into a single overflow dropdown, or show a compact toggle to hide labels.
Marco R.: My vote is an overflow menu that shows the top N (by recent activity) + ‘Show all’. Keeps plot height stable.
Lina K.: Overflow is good but accessibility wise we need keyboard focus and screen reader text for the collapsed label. Maybe aria-label="series legend, collapsed" and a focused menu list.
Jamie T.: Also copy tweak: instead of "Show all" maybe "Expand series" — clearer in context.
Alex M.: Good call. Priya, do we have telemetry to pick the top N? Could use last 7d token contribution to sort.
Priya S.: Yes, we already log series hitcounts. Default top N = 4 seems reasonable for narrow layouts. We can make it config per dashboard.
Marco R.: For very dense charts maybe allow a condensed inline mode: small 8px color swatch + 1-letter abbrev for common series and tooltip on hover. Less visual weight.
Lina K.: Abbrev mode sounds neat but tooltips must be reachable by keyboard (enter/space to reveal) and aria-describedby for SR users.
Jamie T.: Copy nit: the legend tooltip currently says "Units" — product asked to change to "Scale / Units" to avoid confusion for normalized charts.
Alex M.: OK, so implementation plan: 1) Overflow menu fallback with keyboard & SR support; 2) condensed inline variant behind a per-panel toggle "Compact legend"; 3) rename tooltip label to "Scale / Units"; 4) default top N=4 on small widths.
design-bot: Tagging @lina for accessibility review and @priya for telemetry verification. :white_check_mark:
Lina K.: I'll draft the aria spec and keyboard interactions today, will post a tiny diagram.
Priya S.: I'll add the hitcount sorting flag to the dashboard config and a perf test to ensure no extra load.
Alex M.: Awesome — thanks. If nobody objects I'll queue this into the next eng-sprint for a small spike + follow-up design QA. :thumbsup:
